Recently, GPipe further pushes the state-of-the-art ImageNet top-1 validation accuracy to 84.3% using 557M parameters: it is so big that it can only be trained with a specialized pipeline parallelism library by partitioning the network and spreading each part to a different accelerator.
startsectionparagraph4 .5em plus1ex minus.2ex-.5em ConvNet Efficiency: Deep ConvNets are often over-parameterized.

startsectionparagraph4 .5em plus1ex minus.2ex-.5em Model Scaling: There are many ways to scale a ConvNet for different resource constraints: ResNet can be scaled down (e.g., ResNet-18) or up (e.g., ResNet-200) by adjusting network depth (#layers), while WideResNet and MobileNets can be scaled by network width (#channels).
startsectionparagraph4 .5em plus1ex minus.2ex-.5em Depth ( ): Scaling network depth is the most common way used by many ConvNets .
startsectionparagraph4 .5em plus1ex minus.2ex-.5em Width ( ): Scaling network width is commonly used for small size models .
startsectionparagraph4 .5em plus1ex minus.2ex-.5em Resolution ( ): With higher resolution input images, ConvNets can potentially capture more fine-grained patterns.

startsectionparagraph4 .5em plus1ex minus.2ex-.5em Observation 1 -- Scaling up any dimension of network width, depth, or resolution improves accuracy, but the accuracy gain diminishes for bigger models.
If we only scale network width without changing depth ( =1.0) and resolution ( =1.0), the accuracy saturates quickly.
If we only scale network width without changing depth ( =1.0) and resolution ( =1.0), the accuracy saturates quickly.
With deeper ( =2.0) and higher resolution ( =2.0), width scaling achieves much better accuracy under the same FLOPS cost.
With deeper ( =2.0) and higher resolution ( =2.0), width scaling achieves much better accuracy under the same FLOPS cost.

startsectionparagraph4 .5em plus1ex minus.2ex-.5em Observation 2 -- In order to pursue better accuracy and efficiency, it is critical to balance all dimensions of network width, depth, and resolution during ConvNet scaling.

(2) Compared to state-of-the-art models, including DAT that dynamically synthesizes training data and GPipe that is trained with specialized pipeline parallelism, our EfficientNet models still surpass their accuracy in 5 out of 8 datasets, but using 9.6x fewer parameters

In general, all scaling methods improve accuracy with the cost of more FLOPS, but our compound scaling method can further improve accuracy, by up to 2.5%, than other single-dimension scaling methods, suggesting the importance of our proposed compound scaling.
